sup-064316255265a882-0SL1q17:whole.hint: Mark the boundary conditions at both ends, then fit the simplest allowed pattern between them.
notes: Fixed string ends and closed pipe ends are displacement nodes; an open pipe end is a displacement antinode. Adjacent nodes are λ/2 apart; a node and adjacent antinode are λ/4 apart.
Two like ends allow L = nλ/2. One open and one closed end allows L = (2n − 1)λ/4. Use the mode shown, not automatically the fundamental.

duplicate-08a0c6806967acca.hint: Compare oscillation energy at the start and end of the stated interval.
notes: With unchanged mass and natural frequency, total oscillator energy is proportional to amplitude squared. Read the envelope amplitudes at the two times.
Average power lost is (E_initial − E_final)/Δt. A halved amplitude does not mean only half the energy is lost.

Account for any initial phase difference between the sources as well as the path difference. Equivalent phases differ by whole multiples of 2π.

kirk-17476a9c55b97386-q6:whole.hint: The outgoing and reflected microwaves form a stationary pattern. How far apart are neighbouring minima?
notes: The superposition of opposite-travelling waves produces nodes and antinodes. Adjacent intensity minima are separated by half a wavelength.
A node-to-neighbouring-antinode distance is one quarter wavelength; the question asks for minimum to minimum.
